headline: Borrowing by AI companies in the bond market almost stopped in September, and Morgan Stanley expects it to restart this quarter.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: useful hard numbers from one bank's report, relayed by a small outlet.
importance_line: Bond investors and anyone whose pension holds corporate debt got a month's breather from the AI borrowing wave, but if Morgan Stanley is right that the cloud giants will spend about 1.4 trillion dollars in 2027, the debt supply resumes; the numbers are one bank's estimates.
summary: BigGo Finance reports, citing a Morgan Stanley research report, that global AI-related bond sales fell to about 23 billion dollars in September with none at all in the US investment-grade market, after a front-loaded year that had already raised 466 billion dollars, more than double all of 2025. Morgan Stanley calls it "a pause, not a retreat", blaming earlier heavy issuance, permit, power and political obstacles to data centres and rising rates, and expects the big cloud companies to return to the market this quarter as they plan about 1.4 trillion dollars of capital spending for 2027.
notes: Figures are Morgan Stanley's via BigGo Finance; no other outlet found carrying the report.
